title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Premiums Carried by the Hour Band of a Call
content:
Hours the call record puts on a published office holiday carry the tier's holiday multiplier. Hours it
puts outside regular hours, whether on a weekday evening, overnight or at a weekend, carry the tier's
after-hours multiplier. Hours worked in regular hours carry no premium. The multipliers are never compounded. Both multipliers are those published for the program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs.

| Program | Holiday multiplier | After-hours multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| Time & Material Account | 2 | 1.5 |
| Priority Response Program | 2 | 1.5 |
| Block Hour Service Program | 1.75 | 1.5 |
| Emergency Response Program | 1.5 | 1.25 |
| Critical Facility Response Program | 1.5 | 1.25 |
| Dedicated Technician Program | 1.5 | 1.25 |

| The band the call record puts the hours in | The premium those hours carry |
|---|---|
| a published office holiday | the tier's holiday multiplier |
| a weekday evening outside regular hours | the tier's after-hours multiplier |
| overnight | the tier's after-hours multiplier |
| a weekend | the tier's after-hours multiplier |
| regular hours | no premium |

The band is the one the call record carries for the hours worked. Hours the record puts on a published
office holiday carry the holiday multiplier and not, on top of it, the after-hours multiplier, whatever
hour of that holiday they fell in: the multipliers are never compounded, and one band's figure governs
the hours.

**Illustration (hypothetical).** On the Time & Material Account an hour the record puts on a published
office holiday carries a premium of 2.0, and an hour it puts overnight on a weekday carries 1.5. On the
Critical Facility Response Program those two premiums are 1.5 and 1.25 respectively.
